title: Max builds a backyard water tower (and it fights back)

beats.text: One tonne of water, six metres up, on four skinny poles.
Let's rewind to how Max got here.
Max wants a slide that gushes like a real town. Tank on the grass: nothing. Water can't rise above its own surface.
So he lifts it. Every metre adds about 0.1 bar. Six metres: 0.6 bar, and the slide gushes.
Then he fills it: a thousand litres, one tonne. The thin poles bow and fold.
Steel legs, braced into rigid triangles, on concrete footings. The weight goes straight into the ground.
Max switches on the fill pump and grabs a lemonade. Nothing tells the pump to stop, so it spills onto him.
A float valve: the ball rises with the water and shuts the inlet. Plus an overflow pipe.
Max bolts on an airtight lid. The water drains, nothing replaces it, and air crushes the tank.
New tank, screened vent: air flows in as water flows out. Pressure stays equal.
New York still has rooftop tanks like this, because old city pressure ran out around the sixth floor.
The tower feeds the slide, and both kids whoosh down. Gravity does the pumping. Would you build one?
